messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, maze-like decks, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, lighting, music, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement it directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created an original game titled **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, key collection, medkits, charge cells, and a final core boss.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added playable game interface and game implementation in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`.
- Added keyboard, mouse, and touch controls; possession pulse minigame; three decks; items; enemies; boss; health and host decay; canvas lighting and synthesized audio.
- `node --check game.js` passes.
- Opened the game in Playwright and saved screenshots of the title and started game.

### Active
- Review browser console after starting and improve any issues; current browser reports two errors after clicking start, with only the favicon 404 identified before the click.
- Verify gameplay interactions and mobile/touch layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect Playwright console for runtime errors after starting the game.
2. Test movement, firing, possession, key/lift progression, boss fight, and touch controls.
3. Fix any issues and check repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI and HUD.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, rendering, controls, audio.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- A local HTTP server is running at `http://localhost:3002`.
- Screenshots saved as `screenshots/title.jpg` and `screenshots/game.jpg`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, atmosphere, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, supplies, a final core boss, lighting, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented the game interface and mechanics in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`, including keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- Added weighted path carving in `game.js` after testing revealed several authored objectives on decks 2 and 3 were unreachable; verified all authored locations are reachable on all three decks.
- Browser smoke test: starting the game and possessing a host worked with no page or console errors.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Test broader gameplay progression, including combat, lift transitions, boss fight, and mobile/touch layout.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Test movement, firing, possession, key/lift progression, and the final boss in the browser.
2. Check mobile/touch layout and interactions; fix any issues.
3. Recheck repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, map generation, rendering, controls, and audio.
- `screenshots/`: Existing title and gameplay screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- The local game is served at `http://localhost:3002`.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, atmosphere, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, supplies, a final core boss, lighting, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface and mechanics in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`, including keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- Added weighted path carving in `game.js`; authored objectives are reachable on all three decks.
- Browser smoke-tested starting, movement, possession, firing, and medkit input; verified a mobile-sized viewport displays touch controls without horizontal overflow.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Test broader gameplay progression, including key/lift transitions and the final boss fight.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing through the multi-deck progression and boss fight.
2. Fix any issues found and recheck repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, map generation, rendering, controls, and audio.
- `screenshots/`: Existing title and gameplay screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted.
- Local game is served at `http://localhost:3002`.
- The browser reported only a missing `favicon.ico` (404), not a game script error.
- Possession test succeeded; host changed to STALKER, hack overlay closed, and firing/medkit input did not break the game.

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, atmosphere, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, supplies, a final core boss, lighting, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface and mechanics in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`, including keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- Added weighted path carving in `game.js`; authored objectives are reachable on all three decks.
- Browser smoke-tested starting, movement, possession, firing, and medkit input; verified a mobile-sized viewport displays touch controls without horizontal overflow.
- `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` pass.

### Active
- Test multi-deck progression and boss fight. A browser attempt following a computed route did not collect keys; the game remained on deck 1, so movement/path assumptions need investigation.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Inspect actual player coordinates and movement/collision behavior in the browser; fix route testing or gameplay issues found.
2. Continue testing deck transitions and the final boss/win condition.
3. Re-run syntax/diff checks and check repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, map generation, rendering, controls, and audio.
- `screenshots/`: Existing title and gameplay screenshots.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; `git status --short` showed project files as untracked.
- Local game is served at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`.
- Browser console errors were missing favicon requests (`404` for `/favicon.ico`); no game-script error was identified.
- Route attempt remained at deck `01 / 03`, keys `0 / 3`; a later partial movement test showed player minimap position changing.

4: - Do not background them in bounded commands without explicit detachment and cleanup.
5: - After a timeout, inspect the process and endpoint before retrying or claiming failure.

7: ## Linux browser and WebGPU capture
8: 
9: - Use the preinstalled `playwright-cli` executable from Actions or SSH.
10: - Use its headed Chromium, persistent Xvfb display, and SwiftShader configuration.
11: - Run `playwright-cli open http://localhost:3002` for the Pascal development server.
12: - Load a saved scene. Wait for actual geometry and the active WebGPU renderer.
13: - Run `playwright-cli screenshot --filename=screenshots/linux.png` after creating the output directory.
14: - Inspect the image. Reject loading screens, empty grids, and blank canvases.
15: - Report SwiftShader as CPU software rendering. Do not claim GPU hardware acceleration.

  keyup <key>                 press a key up on the keyboard

## Objective
- Build a complete, playable top-down shipboard horror game inspired by *Paradroid* and early *Alien Breed*, with possession, survival supplies, varied hosts, bosses, atmosphere, and touch controls.

## Requirements
- Implement directly in the existing game project; don’t ask clarifying questions.
- Include limited keys, food/medkits, keycards, destructible or possessable enemies, host-specific powers and burnout, multi-floor maze layouts, non-possessable bosses, atmospheric visuals/audio, and touchscreen controls.

## Decisions
- Created **DEAD CHANNEL**, set aboard the derelict salvage vessel Vesper-9.
- Used a self-contained HTML/CSS/Canvas JavaScript implementation with three decks, neural override minigames, host types, supplies, a final core boss, lighting, and synthesized audio.

## Work State
### Completed
- Implemented game interface and mechanics in `index.html`, `style.css`, and `game.js`, including keyboard, mouse, and touch controls.
- Added weighted path carving in `game.js`; authored objectives are reachable on all three decks.
- Browser-tested starting and movement; confirmed the player reaches a key and collects it when positioned at its coordinates.
- Verified `node --check game.js` and `git diff --check` passed earlier.

### Active
- Test progression across decks and the final boss/win condition; the attempted progression check failed due to a malformed browser-eval expression.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing key collection and lift transitions across all decks, then test the core boss and win condition.
2. Remove the temporary `window.__gameDebug` hook from `game.js` after testing.
3. Re-run syntax/diff checks and check repository status.

## Relevant Files
- `index.html`: Game UI, HUD, overlays, and touch controls.
- `style.css`: Desktop and mobile styling.
- `game.js`: Game logic, map generation, rendering, controls, and audio.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the last `git status --short`.
- Local game is served at `http://127.0.0.1:3002/`; the browser session remains open.
- A temporary debug accessor was added at the end of `game.js`: `Object.defineProperty(window,'__gameDebug',{get:()=>game});`.
- Route testing previously remained on deck `01 / 03`, keys `0 / 3`; recent tests confirmed movement and key pickup work when the player reaches a key.

- Implement boss-specific appearances and attack behaviors.

3. Implement boss-specific visuals and attack patterns using the campaign boss metadata.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL from the Vesper-9 into multiple playable ship campaigns, each with a distinct identity and boss.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from a start-screen ship picker; each has a three-deck campaign and boss.
- Campaign concepts include Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions with three floors and distinct boss metadata in `game.js`.
- Added campaign intro placeholders and an empty picker container to `index.html`.
- Updated boss initialization to use the active campaign’s metadata.

### Active
- Integrate campaign selection and campaign-specific UI/game flow.
- Implement boss-specific appearances and attack behaviors.
- Verify campaign starts, progression, and boss encounters.

### Blocked
- (none)

## Next Move
1. Add campaign picker controls and selection logic; set the active campaign’s floors on start and restart.
2. Replace remaining Vesper-9 and hard-coded three-floor assumptions in UI, objectives, boss logic, and end overlays.
3. Implement boss-specific visuals and attack patterns.
4. Test campaign selection, three-deck progression, and boss defeat/victory conditions.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign data, progression, boss setup and behavior.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and campaign intro markup.
- `style.css`: Existing styling; add campaign picker styles.

## Important Context
- The campaign picker has no selection buttons or event handlers yet.
- Game flow still contains Vesper-9-specific text and hard-coded assumptions, including `game.floor===2`, “DESTROY THE CORE,” and fixed three-key progression.
- Changes are unverified. `git status --short` showed project files, including `game.js`, `index.html`, and `style.css`, as untracked.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL beyond Vesper-9 with selectable, playable ship campaigns, each with a distinct identity and boss.
- Review campaign-aware UI and flow, then verify progression, boss encounters, and restart behavior.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions with three floors and distinct boss metadata in `game.js`.
- Added campaign picker controls and selection behavior; campaign title, signal, lineage, intro, blurb, and start button update with selection.
- Made floor/key progression and boss objectives adapt to campaign data.
- Added campaign-specific boss shapes and `fan`, `burst`, and `single` attack patterns.
- Added picker styles in `campaign-picker.css` and linked the stylesheet in `index.html`.
- Updated victory/loss messaging, boss HUD, and restart control for the selected campaign.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Fix and test any campaign selection, restart, progression, boss, or victory-condition issues discovered during browser verification.
- Review remaining Vesper-9-specific UI and hard-coded assumptions; the side-panel crew manifest and hull-pressure details remain Vesper-9-specific.

### Blocked
- Browser-level testing has not been run; Chromium is available, but no browser automation package was detected.

## Next Move
1. Run the game in Chromium and verify picker rendering/selection, each campaign’s three-floor progression, boss attack and defeat, victory, and restart-to-picker behavior.
2. Investigate issues found; audit campaign-specific UI such as the crew manifest and hull-pressure panel for hard-coded Vesper-9 content.
3. Re-run `node --check game.js` and inspect `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign definitions, selection, progression, boss behavior, and rendering.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and campaign-aware UI elements.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Picker layout, responsive behavior, and focus styling.
- `style.css`: Existing game and overlay styling.

## Important Context
- Project files are untracked in the last observed `git status --short`; changes are uncommitted.
- Boss graphics differ by boss kind; attack patterns are shared across kinds based on `single`, `fan`, or `burst`.
- Campaign boss keys are present on the final floor but key progression is disabled there by design.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Implement responsive twin-stick/controller-style controls and make each boss’s randomized attack patterns, minions, and difficulty scale feel distinct and escalate through the game.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with totally different attack patterns, randomized attacks, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as the game progresses.
- Provide independent twin-stick movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit buttons; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign selection UI, campaign-aware progression, distinct boss names/visuals, boss attacks, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Replaced old touch d-pad/actions markup with twin-stick and labeled controller-style buttons; added touch-stick handling, separate link/eject actions, and gamepad polling/mapping.
- Added responsive CSS for virtual sticks and action buttons, replacing styles that targeted removed d-pad markup.

### Active
- Implement boss-specific randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawning, and escalating boss/minion difficulty as the player advances.
- Verify controls and campaign flow, then address any issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser-level verification has not been run; prior context noted Chromium was available but no browser automation package was detected.

## Next Move
1. Add distinct randomized attack behaviors and minion-spawn logic for each campaign boss, with difficulty scaling by deck/progression regardless of campaign.
2. Run `node --check game.js`; inspect gamepad polling, repeated fire behavior, and control input.
3. Verify campaign selection, progression, boss encounters, victory, restart, and controls; inspect `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign/boss definitions, progression, combat, controls, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker, control hint, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive twin-stick and controller button styling.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the last observed `git status --short`.
- Existing boss definitions use `kind`, `pattern`, and campaign-specific HP, but behavior is currently limited to single shots, fans, or bursts; no boss minion spawning or progression scaling has been implemented.
- Crew manifest and hull-pressure panel remain Vesper-9-specific.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Provide responsive twin-stick/controller-style controls, randomized boss attacks and minions, and escalating difficulty as players progress.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with different attack patterns, randomized attacks, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as the game progresses.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct boss names/visuals, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, and action mappings with responsive styling.
- Added distinct randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types in `game.js`.
- Added difficulty scaling for boss health and attack damage/speed, and enemy health/movement/fire rate across decks.

### Active
- Finish integrating boss minion spawning into the boss update loop; `spawnBossMinion()` exists but is not yet called.
- Verify controls, campaign flow, combat, and difficulty; fix any issues found.

### Blocked
- Browser-level verification has not been run; prior context noted Chromium was available but no browser automation package was detected.

## Next Move
1. Integrate periodic, capped minion spawning in the boss update loop, with deck-based escalation and suitable cooldowns.
2. Run `node --check game.js`; inspect attack cadence, projectile balance, minion behavior, and control input.
3. Verify campaign selection, progression, boss encounters, victory, restart, and controls; inspect `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaigns, progression, combat, boss patterns/minions, controls, and game loop.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive twin-stick and action-button styling.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

## Important Context
- Changes are uncommitted; project files were untracked in the last observed `git status --short`.
- `game.js` now contains `spawnBossBullet()`, eight distinct `bossVolley()` pattern cases, and `spawnBossMinion()`; the minion-spawn function is not yet wired into `update()`.
- Crew manifest and hull-pressure panel remain Vesper-9-specific.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Provide responsive twin-stick/controller-style controls, randomized boss attacks and minions, and escalating difficulty.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with different attack patterns, randomized attacks, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, fire, and face-button actions with responsive styling.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- Verified in headless Chromium: all eight campaigns render, campaign selection updates campaign labels and start button, starting a campaign enters gameplay, and mobile viewport shows both sticks and action buttons without horizontal overflow.
- Chromium verification reported no JavaScript exceptions; mobile screenshot saved at `/tmp/opencode/dead-channel-mobile.png`.
- `node --check game.js` passed after the latest code edits.

### Active
- Verify multi-deck progression, boss encounters, minion behavior, victory/restart, and input mappings; address any issues found.

### Blocked
- Full browser-driven combat/progression verification is still incomplete; the initial Chromium check only covered campaign selection, starting gameplay, and mobile layout.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser verification through deck progression, boss combat and minion spawning, victory/restart, and keyboard/gamepad/touch controls.
2. Fix any gameplay or UI issues found.
3. Check `git status --short`; project files are untracked.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign definitions, progression, combat, boss patterns/minions, and controls.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and twin-stick controls.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

## Important Context
- Boss minion cap is `1 + game.floor`; boss defeat removes remaining minions.
- Headless Chromium was launched with remote debugging on port `9222`; the mobile screenshot is at `/tmp/opencode/dead-channel-mobile.png`.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Ensure twin-stick/controller-style controls, randomized boss attacks and minions, and escalating difficulty work correctly.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, fire, and face-button actions with responsive styling.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- `node --check game.js` passed. Browser loaded at `http://localhost:8765/`; page snapshot showed the expected title screen and all eight campaign choices.

### Active
- Finish end-to-end browser verification of deck progression, boss combat/minions, victory/restart, and keyboard/gamepad/touch input.

- (none)

1. Click `#startButton` in the browser and explicitly confirm `game.started === true`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign definitions, progression, combat, boss patterns/minions, and controls.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and twin-stick controls.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

- Boss minion cap is `1 + game.floor`.

messages.summary:
## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Ensure twin-stick/controller-style controls, randomized boss attacks and minions, and escalating difficulty work correctly.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, fire, and face-button actions with responsive styling.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- `node --check game.js` passed.
- Browser loaded at `http://localhost:8765/`; page rendered the title screen and eight campaign choices.
- Clicking `#startButton` successfully began gameplay; intro overlay hid, status updated to “Insertion complete. Find the access keys.”, and objective showed “FIND 3 ACCESS KEYS”.
- Browser console errors were only failed `/favicon.ico` requests (404).

### Active
- Complete end-to-end browser verification of deck transitions, boss combat/minion cap, victory/restart, and keyboard/gamepad/touch input.
- The latest `playwright-cli run-code` test failed to parse (`SyntaxError: Unexpected identifier 'page'`); no further gameplay or control verification was achieved.

### Blocked
- Browser test snippets passed to `playwright-cli run-code` have had syntax errors, so automated in-game state verification remains incomplete.

## Next Move
1. Use supported Playwright CLI commands or valid `run-code` syntax to start the game and confirm live gameplay state.
2. Verify key collection and deck transitions, boss scaling/attacks/minion cap, boss defeat and victory, restart, and keyboard/gamepad/touch mappings.
3. Fix confirmed issues and check `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaign definitions, progression, combat, boss patterns/minions, and controls.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and twin-stick controls.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

## Important Context
- Boss minion cap is `1 + game.floor`.
- `playwright-cli eval` can evaluate an expression, but the prior `run-code` snippets failed with syntax errors.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files showed as untracked. No commit or push was made.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Verify controls, randomized boss combat and minions, and escalating difficulty through end-to-end gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, fire, and face-button actions with responsive styling.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser loaded at `http://localhost:8765/`, displayed all eight campaigns, and successfully started Odyssey Array gameplay.
- Verified objective/deck/status display, WASD movement via minimap, and responsive touch controls at 390×844; controls are hidden at desktop width.

### Active
- Finish end-to-end verification of key collection and deck transitions, boss attacks/scaling/minion cap, boss defeat, victory/restart, aiming/firing, touch interactions, and gamepad mappings where practical.
- Inspect and fix any confirmed gameplay issues; check `git status --short`.

### Blocked
- Browser combat verification remains unfinished; prior movement testing caused health to drop to 24% before reaching objectives.
- No known hard blocker.

## Next Move
1. Continue browser testing with safe routes and medkits; verify key pickup and deck transitions.
2. Exercise boss combat, attack variety, minion cap, defeat/victory, and restart; test aiming/fire and touch/gamepad controls where practical.
3. Fix confirmed issues, rerun checks, and inspect `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaigns, progression, combat, bosses/minions, and control handlers.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and twin-stick controls.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

## Important Context
- Boss minion cap is `1 + game.floor`.
- Browser console showed failed `/favicon.ico` requests (404).
- `playwright-cli run-code` expects a JavaScript function, e.g. `playwright-cli run-code "async page => { ... }"`.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files were reported as untracked. No commit or push was made.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable, playable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns and distinct bosses.
- Verify controls, randomized boss combat and minions, and escalating difficulty through end-to-end gameplay.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Touch controls use two virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; gamepad mapping uses standard face buttons and triggers.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added twin-stick touch controls and standard gamepad movement, aiming, fire, and face-button actions with responsive styling.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- `node --check game.js` passed; browser confirmed eight campaigns, key collection, first deck transition, eight boss patterns producing projectiles, floor-3 minion cap, boss defeat/minion cleanup, and victory.
- Browser verified touch link sequence, medkit, eject, visible controls, and gamepad movement, firing, and medkit.
- Browser verified virtual-stick movement and aiming; restart returned to the campaign picker.

### Active
- Correct and rerun touch virtual-stick firing and gamepad aiming checks; prior assertions were inconclusive because the test left the player as an unarmed Wraith and checked the wrong aim axis.
- Verify campaign selection by clicking a non-default campaign, and test remaining deck transitions where practical.
- Inspect and fix confirmed gameplay issues; rerun `node --check game.js` and inspect `git status --short`.

### Blocked
- No current blocker. The earlier `.hack-inputs` selector failure was resolved with shell-safe quoting.

## Next Move
1. Rerun input tests with a weapon-bearing host for aim/fire, and assert the aim direction on the correct axis.
2. Explicitly click Odyssey Array (or another non-default campaign) before checking its `aria-pressed` state; test later deck transitions where practical.
3. Run `node --check game.js`, inspect `git status --short`, and address any confirmed issues.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaigns, progression, combat, bosses/minions, and control handlers.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Responsive layout and twin-stick controls.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker styling.

- Boss minion cap is `1 + game.floor`.
- Browser is at `http://localhost:8765/`; console previously reported a `/favicon.ico` 404.
- Changes remain uncommitted; project files are reported as untracked. No commit or push was made.

## Objective
- Expand DEAD CHANNEL with selectable science-fiction-inspired ship campaigns, three-deck progression, randomized bosses/minions, and escalating difficulty.
- Provide the requested Xbox/PlayStation-style twin-stick controls and button layout; the user says the existing controls do not match what they asked for.

## Requirements
- Include loosely inspired campaigns spanning Star Trek, Star Wars, Farscape, Babylon 5, Space: 1999, and other science-fiction settings.
- Give every ship a unique boss with randomized attack patterns, occasional minion spawns, and increasing toughness/difficulty as players progress.
- Support independent movement and aiming, plus Xbox/PlayStation-style action buttons.
- User’s latest request: “Update the existing checkpoint in the conversation above into one consolidated summary.” This is now satisfied; their prior control complaint remains to be addressed in the code.

## Decisions
- Campaigns are selected from the start-screen ship picker; each has three decks and a boss.
- Campaign concepts: Vesper-9, Meridian, Ashen Crown, Manta-class Living Ship, Citadel Nine, Selene Outpost, Pelagic, and Odyssey Array.
- Prior implementation used touch virtual sticks and A/✕ link, B/○ eject, X/□ medkit; the user says this is not the twin-stick/controller-style layout they requested.

## Work State
### Completed
- Added eight campaign definitions, three-floor progression, campaign picker, campaign-aware progression, distinct bosses, and victory/loss/restart messaging.
- Added randomized projectile patterns for all eight boss types, scaling difficulty, and periodic capped boss minions removed on boss defeat.
- Browser checks confirmed campaign selection, transitions through all three decks, boss patterns/minion cap, boss defeat cleanup, victory, touch link/eject/medkit, virtual-stick movement/aim/fire, and gamepad movement/aim/fire/medkit.
- `node --check game.js` passed.

### Active
- Reconcile and implement the requested Xbox/PlayStation-style twin-stick control layout. Inspect existing touch controls and the user’s intended button placement/semantics; the prior implementation’s three labeled touch action buttons plus twin virtual sticks was rejected by the user as not matching their ask.
- Recheck touch and gamepad mappings and layout after changes.

### Blocked
- Exact desired “button layout” is not specified in the latest message, which ends mid-sentence (“…and the button layo…”). Clarify from context or ask the user before assuming the action layout.

## Next Move
1. Inspect `index.html`, `style.css`, `game.js`, and `campaign-picker.css` for current touch-control structure and mappings.
2. Determine/clarify the intended Xbox/PlayStation twin-stick face-button layout before changing action-button arrangement; ensure left stick moves and right stick aims/fires.
3. Implement and browser-test the corrected layout, then rerun `node --check game.js` and inspect `git status --short`.

## Relevant Files
- `game.js`: Campaigns, progression, boss/minion combat, keyboard, touch, and gamepad handlers.
- `index.html`: Campaign picker, game overlays, and touch-control markup.
- `style.css`: Main responsive layout.
- `campaign-picker.css`: Campaign picker and overlay styling.

## Important Context
- Prior browser verification of aim/fire used a weapon-bearing host; gamepad aim is asserted on the correct axis.
- Browser was at `http://localhost:8765/`; console previously reported a `/favicon.ico` 404.
- Project files remain uncommitted and appear untracked in `git status --short`.
